source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #260 (branch fix/240-fn-identity at merge commit 5e83bf5733738214d30c7d31d5487b812cc0df03 — branch head 96cc96fd1170deb60e45c4b4dab2b8252958b6c1 with current main 5d6bc720f2281a79818dba879dcd3e67c6bdd280 merged in without conflicts, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45089043304 and 45089382531 against the branch and pull-request run 45088697826, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #260 (#240, pin fn-pointer handler identity against duplication and identical-code folding). The PR marks all 512 identity-compared op handlers #[inline(never)] so the compiler cannot duplicate them across codegen units, adds identity barriers (a function-local static whose address is passed to core::hint::black_box) to the byte-identical twin handlers — the shared/indexed load/store template families in crates/telomere/src/runtime/vm/memory.rs, op_f32_store / op_f64_store, and op_return in crates/telomere/src/runtime/vm/control.rs — documents the identity contract on Op in crates/telomere/src/common.rs, and adds tools/check-fn-identity.py (wired into CI) with its unit tests plus OP_SPECS decode tests. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (5d6bc72) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45089386493, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 28 gated series, so every delta is this PR’s own. Growth appears in every configuration that links the telomere library and is near-uniform, as expected when 512 handler bodies stop being inlined into or merged with their dispatch sites: release stripped file +15,008..+22,864 B and stripped .text +13,952..+21,184 B (core-jit grows most because it also links the JIT backend handlers annotated in crates/telomere/src/runtime/jit/backend/ops.rs); release-size (opt-level z, fat LTO, one codegen unit) stripped file +9,040..+9,776 B and stripped .text +10,512..+11,936 B. The baseline configuration (no library) is byte-identical in both profiles, so 4 of 28 gated series are unchanged and 24 move. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3; the raw file and .text sizes were also identical across the three runs), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, ‘Size regression gate (#164)’.
